content: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) are recommended as the first-line treatment for patients who have both diabetes and coronary artery disease. These medications are particularly effective in reducing the risk of progressive kidney disease in individuals with a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) of 30 mg/g or higher. Additionally, they play a critical role in preserving kidney function by lowering the incidence of cardiovascular events in patients with chronic kidney disease.
